observations: A thick white X sits over the right side of the face, crossing olive-green and teal lines that fill that area.
A red oval mouth near the bottom center holds jagged yellow-green tooth-like marks, outlined by a bright pink lip shape.
Lime-green and yellow hatched lines spray outward from the top of the head, layered over purple lines that loosely frame the skull shape.
reading: Heavy black lines carve a nose bridge and brow, but color escapes everywhere—cyan curls at the throat, magenta along the jaw, yellow above the crown. The white X over one eye area can read as a cancellation or a wound. The open red mouth, with its crude teeth, holds something between a shout and a grin, leaving the mood unresolved. A flat gray field isolates the figure starkly.
contextAngle: In the owned Scrimshaw subset, this sits between "Scrimshaw 33" and "Scrimshaw 41" by title number. Both neighbors build head-like forms from dense overlapping lines, but this work's flat gray background isolates the figure more sharply than the dark fields surrounding its neighbors.

connections.reason: Both show bared teeth inside a red-outlined mouth, but Scrimshaw 41 uses white zigzag teeth on a dark ground while this work uses yellow-green marks against pink.
Both place a face on a gray background with crossed-out eye areas; the nnxyz work uses red X hatching in squared sockets, while this work uses a single bold white X.

lookingQuestion: Where do the purple framing lines begin and end—do they outline the whole head, or do they break apart, and what happens to the figure where they disappear?
ambiguities: Whether the white X functions as an eye or as an overlay mark placed on top of the face cannot be determined from the image alone.
The teal spiral cluster at the lower throat area may be a separate element or an extension of the face's line network.
